content.title: About
content.content: Whole grain reduced-fat pancakes are a ready‑to‑mix blend of whole‑grain flour, skimmed milk and a small amount of plant oil. They retain the classic pancake flavor while providing more fiber and less fat, making them a healthier choice for breakfast or a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole‑grain flour keeps the bran and germ, boosting B‑vitamins and minerals.
Reduced fat is achieved by using skimmed milk and less oil in the recipe.
The batter cooks quickly – just add water, stir, and fry on a non‑stick pan.
Traditionally pancakes are a symbol of the Russian Maslenitsa festival; the whole‑grain version makes the tradition healthier.
The mix can be stored in a dry place for up to 12 months.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain flour supplies dietary fiber that supports regular bowel movements and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Reduced fat content helps control calorie intake, useful for weight management.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and niacin aid energy metabolism and support the nervous system.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Iron, magnesium and zinc are present, contributing to blood health and muscle function.

items.title: Supports blood‑sugar stability
items.content: Fiber slows glucose absorption, helping to avoid rapid blood‑sugar spikes after meals.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Whole‑grain flour contains gluten, so the product is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some mixes may contain added salt; those monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Bacterial growth risk
items.content: If batter is left at room temperature for more than 2 hours, bacterial growth can occur; prepare only the portion you will cook immediately.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dilute the mix with water (or plant‑based milk) as directed, pour thin layers onto a non‑stick skillet without extra oil, and cook until golden. Serve with fresh berries, low‑fat yogurt, nut butter or a drizzle of honey.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the mix in a cool, dry place, tightly sealed. After opening, use within 3‑4 weeks. Protect from moisture to prevent clumping and spoilage.

content.title: About
content.content: Sweet potato (batata) is a starchy root vegetable rich in carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals. Boiling retains most nutrients, giving it a soft texture and a mildly sweet flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet potato belongs to the Convolvulaceae family and is not related to regular potato.
It is high in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Around the world batata is prepared in many ways: boiled, baked, fried, and used in desserts.
Several cultivars exist with flesh ranging from white to bright orange and purple.
Batata was domesticated in Central and South America over 5,000 years ago.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: The orange flesh provides a high amount of provitamin A, supporting vision and immune function.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Complex carbohydrates supply steady energy and promote satiety.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, helps regulate blood sugar, and supports gut microbiome health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Sweet potato provides vitamin B6, thiamine, and niacin, important for metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Potassium, magnesium, and iron in sweet potato contribute to heart and muscle function.

items.title: High glycemic index after boiling
items.content: Boiled sweet potato can raise blood glucose quickly, so people with diabetes should watch portion sizes.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may be allergic to sweet potato.

items.title: Skin considerations
items.content: If the skin is left on, pesticide residues may remain; wash thoroughly before cooking.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boiled sweet potato can be eaten on its own, added to salads, soups, mashed, or used as a filling for wraps. Cut into cubes for quick snacks or blend into smoothies.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store boiled sweet potato in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze portioned pieces—they retain flavor and nutrients.

content.title: About
content.content: Green iced tea is a ready‑to‑drink beverage made from brewed green tea, chilled and sweetened with sugar. It features a light vegetal aroma, refreshing taste, and moderate sweetness.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green tea is rich in polyphenols, which have antioxidant properties.
Cooling the tea retains most of the beneficial compounds found in hot brews.
Sweetening with sugar makes the drink more appealing to children but adds calories.
Green tea has been traditionally consumed in East Asian cultures for its health benefits.
Iced tea is often served with lemon or lime wedges for extra flavor.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Polyphenols in green tea help combat free radicals and may reduce the risk of chronic diseases.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: Caffeine and L‑theanine can boost metabolic rate and aid calorie burning.

items.title: Improved focus
items.content: The combination of caffeine and L‑theanine promotes alertness without a sharp energy spike.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Iced tea provides a refreshing source of fluid, especially in hot weather.

items.title: Stress reduction
items.content: L‑theanine promotes relaxation and may lower stress levels.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Added sugar increases calories and can affect blood glucose levels.

items.title: Caffeine
items.content: Excessive intake may cause insomnia, anxiety, or rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Tea allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to tea components.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Tea can slightly increase stomach acidity, which may be problematic for gastritis sufferers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the chilled green tea over ice, optionally adding a slice of lemon or fresh mint. It works as a refreshing daily beverage or as part of a sports nutrition routine.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bottle or can refrigerated at 0‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 3‑5 days. Do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
